claims.statement: Application::start_recording enforces a single active recording at the application layer: it holds a tokio mutex over active_recording across the whole native call, refuses reentry with RECORDING_BUSY, mints the recording id with Uuid::now_v7, stores the id only if the native start succeeded, and stop/cancel verify the requested id against the stored one (RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH or RECORDING_NOT_ACTIVE) and clear the slot once the native call returns, even when it fails.

The application-layer test recording_lifecycle_rejects_reentry_and_wrong_session pins the recording lifecycle: a second start fails with RECORDING_BUSY, stopping a foreign id fails with RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH, a valid stop succeeds, and restart plus cancel work afterwards.

NativeRecorder implements the RecordingPort port and runs start/stop/cancel inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking to keep audio-device and filesystem work off the async runtime; it independently enforces the single-recording invariant (RECORDING_BUSY) and verifies the recording id in take_recording before yielding the session, making it the sole owner of the ActiveRecording slot.

A recording immediately owns its meeting folder: start_sync creates the output root, then creates a folder named by recording_folder_name() as 'YYYY-MM-DD HHMMSS 녹음' before touching audio, and targets folder_name/folder_name.wav.part so the finished WAV and all later artifacts share one predictable name.

The transcription path's create_meeting_directory recognizes the recording layout: an input at {stem}/{stem}.wav whose parent already equals output_root/{stem} reuses that folder as the meeting folder, so the SRT, speaker text, checkpoint, and minutes produced later land next to the finished WAV.

Capture is microphone-only by design: NativeRecorder opens only the CPAL default host's default_input_device (MICROPHONE_UNAVAILABLE when absent) and its default_input_config; system audio such as Zoom or Meet calls is not captured, which the README documents as a product constraint and troubleshooting answer rather than a bug.

capture::build dispatches on the device's concrete CPAL SampleFormat and funnels every supported format to i16: integer formats convert via FromSample while f32/f64 clamp to the i16 range with non-finite values mapped to 0, rejecting unsupported formats with UNSUPPORTED_AUDIO_CONFIG.

The CPAL input callback never blocks: enqueue converts input into FRAMES_PER_CHUNK (4096) frame chunks, reuses buffers from the writer's recycle channel and allocates only when the pool is empty, sends nonblockingly with try_send into a sync_channel sized for about 30 seconds of audio, counts samples dropped when the queue is full into an AtomicU64 instead of failing, and short-circuits once a failure is recorded.

CPAL stream errors are classified: ErrorKind::Xrun (a CoreAudio overrun) is treated as recoverable and ignored, while any other stream error records a MICROPHONE_DISCONNECTED failure; a test pins both branches.

writer::spawn creates the .wav.part exclusively with create_new(true), wraps it in a hound WavWriter with a 16-bit int spec, and runs the named galpi-wav-writer thread behind a bounded command channel; if opening the file, building the writer, or spawning the thread fails, the just-created file is removed, escalating to RECORDING_CLEANUP_FAILED when even removal fails.

The writer loop appends silence for dropped samples so the timeline stays continuous, guards the 4GB PCM limit (samples*2 exceeding RIFF_DATA_LIMIT = u32::MAX - 44 records WAV_TOO_LARGE and stops accepting data), writes chunks through hound's bulk i16 writer to skip per-sample checks, returns each buffer to the recycle channel, and flushes roughly every five seconds of audio to bound crash loss.

WriterHandle::finish and cancel perform a synchronous command/reply handshake and join the writer thread; Finish appends trailing dropped silence, finalizes the WAV header, and replies with WriterSummary { samples, dropped_samples }, Cancel drops the writer leaving the partial file for the caller, and a dead writer or join panic maps to WAV_WRITER_FAILED.

Writer tests pin the durable file contract: writes_exact_pcm_samples_and_header verifies byte-exact samples and the WAV spec, and fills_dropped_samples_with_silence_and_reports_them verifies dropped samples become zeros ([0,0,1,2,0,0] for dropped_before=2, samples=[1,2], finish(2)) with dropped_samples=4 in the summary.

recording/failure.rs implements a first-failure-wins slot with two emission modes: set_failure stores and emits a RecordingFailure through the RecordingEvents port but is only for callers off the audio thread, while record_failure stores the state without emitting so the realtime callback stays off IPC; has_failure lets the callback check with one acquire load, and take_failure drains the slot for the stop path.

Recording failures reach the UI as recording-event Tauri events emitted by TauriEvents' RecordingEvents implementation, and the frontend subscribes via TauriBackend.listenToRecordingFailures, which Zod-parses the payload into a RecordingFailure before handing it to the controller.

stop_sync drains the shared failure slot after the writer finishes: any failure recorded during the recording (writer death, WAV_TOO_LARGE, microphone disconnection) turns the stop into an error and removes the partial file, so the stop reply still reports a native failure even if the UI missed the recording-event emission.

Stop derives the result from the written stream, not wall time: frames = samples/channels, duration_seconds = frames/sample_rate (a u32 overflow fails with WAV_TOO_LARGE), dropped_frames = dropped_samples/channels; the .wav.part is atomically renamed to folder_name.wav and canonicalized, every error branch removes the partial, and cleanup failures merge into the original error as RECORDING_CLEANUP_FAILED via with_cleanup.

Cancel verifies the recording id, drops the stream, cancels the writer (joined), and removes the .wav.part; remove_partial also removes the meeting folder with plain remove_dir, which succeeds only when the folder is empty, so a folder that already accumulated artifacts survives.

Teardown is belt-and-braces so a .wav.part never outlives the session: Drop for NativeRecorder (when the last Arc to its state is released) takes any still-active recording, stops the stream, cancels the writer, and removes the partial, logging failures to stderr, while RecordingController.dispose cancels any active recording over IPC when the frontend controller shuts down.

power.rs SleepBlocker is an RAII guard over the macOS PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertion acquired after the stream starts playing with the name 'Galpi meeting recording in progress'; it is stored in ActiveRecording, so it is released exactly when the recording ends (stop, cancel, failure teardown, or process shutdown), and acquire returning None means recording continues without sleep protection with a stderr note.

RecordingController buffers native failures that race the start call: events arriving while status is 'starting' are held in pendingFailures keyed by recording id, and once start resolves the controller looks up the fresh id and, if an early failure is waiting, runs cleanupFailure — cancelling the recording over IPC (which natively removes the partial file) and rendering the failed state; a test pins this exact interleaving.

The elapsed clock is computed from the session start (nowMs - startedAtMs) rather than counting ticks, so webview timer throttling in the background loses nothing; the controller adds visibilitychange and focus listeners as catch-up moments, and a tick that only advances the clock takes the narrow setRecordingTime path, leaving the rest of the recorder view untouched.

A successful stop auto-selects the finished WAV as the transcription input: RecordingController passes result.path into the selectAudio callback wired by AppController (setting the app's audio path and view), and completeRecordingState settles elapsedSeconds on the recorder-reported durationSeconds (not the wall clock) and sets the warning flag when droppedFrames > 0, telling the user missing audio was replaced by silence.

The wire contract reports frames and drops: RecordingStatus carries recordingId, the partial path, sampleRate, and channels, while RecordingResult extends it with frames, droppedFrames, and durationSeconds (camelCase serialization on the host, Zod schemas recordingStatusSchema/recordingResultSchema on the frontend).

composition.rs is the only place NativeRecorder is wired: the same TauriEvents instance serves as both JobEvents and RecordingEvents, and NativeRecorder is installed as the sole production RecordingPort behind the Application facade.
